artifacts.summary: All 4 plan phases completed: --reap mode added to the writer, writer-level and hook-level fixture coverage added, the SessionStart hook restructured for an ungated cross-project reap pass, and documentation/redeploy/live verification completed with no wrongful reap.

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a --reap cross-project action to setup-sapience-mcp.sh and restructured the SessionStart hook to invoke it unconditionally on every session start, closing the gap where a deleted/renamed project's sapience MCP registration could never be reaped. All 4 plan phases completed and committed individually; 36-case test suite green in both the source store and the deployed tree; live ~/.claude.json census confirmed no wrongful reap.

memory_candidates.content: When adding a cross-cutting standalone action to a shell writer/hook pair where the hook must invoke the action unconditionally regardless of its own per-repo gating: (1) in the writer, place the new action's dispatch alongside any existing standalone-action short-circuits (e.g. --retire-global), before any top-level hard-exit resource resolution the new action doesn't need; (2) in the hook, hoist every precondition the new action shares with the existing per-repo logic (jq presence, writer existence) above the per-repo gating branch, convert that branch's early-exit arms into a boolean flag instead, and replace a single-NOTICE tail with an array-based notice assembly so any subset of independent notice sources still yields exactly one output line.

deploy-headless.sh's inline verify-deploy.sh call defaults to --skip-slow (opt-out via --skip-verify suppresses it entirely), which is a lighter-weight gate pass distinct from an independent full-depth verify-deploy.sh invocation. Under a Batch Gate Deferral directive that prohibits running the complete gate set a second time, a plan phase whose own task list mandates 'redeploy via deploy-headless.sh' can treat that script's own built-in --skip-slow pass as the scoped discharge for a 'verify-deploy.sh green' verification criterion, rather than needing a separate narrowing invocation.

sapience_notes.subject: task 627 orphan sapience MCP registration
sapience_notes.value: The task description's cited stale /home/benjamin/Projects/sapience-app registration (.mcpServers.sapience on a deleted-path row) was already gone by the time research ran -- the row existed but carried mcpServers:{} with no sapience subkey. Re-confirmed at implementation time: zero orphaned sapience registrations existed across all live .projects rows throughout this task's entire lifecycle, so live acceptance was always a no-wrongful-reap regression check rather than a reproducible repro; the real discriminating evidence lived entirely in fixture-based test cases.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh inline verification depth
sapience_notes.value: deploy-headless.sh's own inline verify-deploy.sh call runs with --skip-slow by default (an opt-out --skip-verify flag suppresses it entirely), which is measurably lighter than an independent full-depth verify-deploy.sh invocation and does not trigger Gate 8's shell-suite battery mutex contention the way an unflagged full run would.

sapience_notes.subject: bash array expansion under set -uo pipefail
sapience_notes.value: In this machine's bash, `"${arr[@]}"` expansion on a declared-but-empty array under `set -u` (no -e) does not raise an unbound-variable error -- confirmed empirically via both setup-sapience-mcp.sh's orphans array and sapience-mcp-register-project.sh's NOTICES array, each gated by a `${#arr[@]} -eq 0` check before any loop/printf expansion, with no bash-version-specific guard needed beyond that check.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh Containment Self-Check and __WHOLE_TREE__
sapience_notes.value: git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check treats the __WHOLE_TREE__ file_scope sentinel as a literal pathspec string, not a semantic wildcard that widens containment to every path. A path outside the task's explicitly-listed file_scope entries (e.g. an auto-regenerated index file touched incidentally by a whole-tree redeploy) is still dropped from the phase commit and must be landed via a separate git-commit-scoped.sh follow-up commit, even when __WHOLE_TREE__ is itself present in the declared file_scope.

sapience_notes.subject: test fixture design for bidirectional assertions
sapience_notes.value: Merging two directional test assertions (e.g. 'an orphan row is correctly reaped' and 'a live row survives untouched') into a single shared fixture and invocation, rather than two separate cases, keeps a growing regression suite's case count tighter without losing discriminating power -- both directions are proven by one --reap call against a fixture containing both an orphan and a present-path row.
